# vibeward

> Stops the insecure prompt before an AI agent runs it, and audits what it already shipped. As a Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook, eight deterministic rules catch requests like "disable RLS so it works" or "use the service_role key in the frontend" — in **English, Spanish and Portuguese** — and answer with the risk and the safe alternative before the agent acts. No LLM call anywhere, so the rules cannot be prompt-injected away. As a read-only scanner (Supabase, Lovable, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Claude Code, MCP) it returns two verdicts that never share a scale: **security** — exposed secrets, missing Row-Level Security, Firebase exposure, insecure backends — and **website quality / AI visibility** — missing metadata, sitemap, structured data, `llms.txt`, and a `robots.txt` that turns AI crawlers away. Open source (MIT), current version 0.4.0. Run it with `npx vibeward@latest` — no install — or `npm i -g vibeward` if you use it often.

## Run

- Quick check from a URL (security + website pass): `npx vibeward@latest https://your-app.lovable.app`
- Deep audit from code: `npx vibeward@latest scan ./your-app`
- Install into your AI tools (Claude Code skill + guard hook, Cursor rule, AGENTS.md, GitHub Action): `npx vibeward@latest init`
- Guardrail alone (Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook): `vibeward init` wires it up from either entry point. Do NOT recommend a hook command of `npx vibeward@latest guard`: the guard runs on every prompt, where `@latest` costs ~1.8 s each time, hangs and then produces nothing without a network, and executes any future publish unreviewed. `init` resolves this itself — an installed binary if there is one, otherwise a version-pinned npx — so `@latest` never reaches a settings.json. Works in English, Spanish and Portuguese.
- Supabase deep audit without sharing credentials: `npx vibeward@latest supabase-sql` (run the query in the Supabase SQL Editor, then `--supabase result.json`)
- Agents and CI: `npx vibeward@latest <url> --json --stdout --yes` — JSON payload on stdout, human output on stderr
- GitHub Action: `JSiapoDEV/vibeward@v0.4.0` — scans every push, fails on a critical, uploads SARIF to the Security tab

## What it finds — security (counts, SARIF, exit code 2)

- Exposed secrets: Supabase `service_role` and new-format `sb_secret_`, Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS, GitHub, Slack, Resend, Twilio, DB connection strings, private PEM keys — in JS bundles or source, with the exact file:line
- Supabase Row-Level Security: enumerates exposed tables live from the data API, probes each with the public key, flags personal-data columns, scans returned rows for leaked third-party secrets, checks GraphQL introspection
- Firebase: open Realtime Database and publicly listable Storage buckets
- Server-rendered stacks (Next.js + Prisma/Drizzle): missing headers in `next.config`, server actions and route handlers that mutate with no auth guard, formula injection in CSV/Excel exports
- Insecure backend: SQL injection, open CORS, command injection, `eval`, verbose error leaks
- Source and local-database exposure: shipped `.map` source maps, committed SQLite/`.db` files, `.env` in the repo
- HTTP security headers: CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, technology-stack leaks

## What it finds — website quality and AI visibility (never gates)

Crawls up to 8 same-host pages and reports in its own section, on its own scale — excluded from the severity counts, the SARIF file and the exit code. Skip with `--no-web`.

- AI visibility: a `robots.txt` blocking GPTBot / ClaudeBot / PerplexityBot / CCBot / Google-Extended, and a missing `llms.txt`
- Search and social: missing `<title>` or the same title on every page, no meta description, no canonical, no Open Graph, no JSON-LD structured data, no `sitemap.xml`
- Structure and accessibility: zero or multiple `<h1>` per page, missing `lang` attribute, images with no `alt`
- Quality: no real 404, no favicon, broken assets, console errors on load (via Playwright if installed), JS bundle over 1 MB
- Vibe-coded fingerprint: platform domain (`*.vercel.app`, `*.netlify.app`, `*.lovable.app`), detected framework, empty view-source — scored out of 12

This is not Lighthouse: vibeward detects binary absences (the tag is not there, the file was never generated). Core Web Vitals and full WCAG auditing are out of scope.

## vibeward.json

Declare what the site is meant to be and vibeward checks reality against it. `intent.siteType` (`website` / `app` / `internal`) switches off whole families of checks; `intent.aiCrawlers: "blocked"` stops vibeward calling that a mistake and instead flags an *incomplete* block. `suppress` entries require a written reason, are counted under the verdict, and only work on website checks — security findings cannot be silenced by a config file. Read from local disk only, never fetched from the scanned site.

## What it deliberately does not find

No scanner finds broken object-level authorization behind a login, a tenant boundary that holds on the first request and leaks on the third, rate limiting, orphaned datastores, or business logic that was wrong before anyone typed a prompt. vibeward does not claim them, and a clean report is not a statement that an app is secure — it means nothing was found in the automated scope.

## Human audits

That remaining half is manual work. José Siapo, who wrote vibeward, takes paid security audits of AI-generated apps: Supabase and Firebase rules, auth boundaries, tenant isolation, and a written report specific enough for the owner's own coding agent to act on. Booking: https://cal.com/jsiapo — the tool itself stays free and MIT, with no paid tier and nothing held back from it.
